title: Robert Downey Jr. explains how Doctor Doom differs from Tony Stark
excerpt:
Downey wants Victor von Doom to stand on his own.
Avengers: Doomsday opens December 18, 2026.
body_md:
Robert Downey Jr. has offered fresh insight into his approach to playing Victor von Doom in Avengers: Doomsday, less than a month before the film reaches theaters. The actor's return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe in a villainous role has raised questions ever since the casting announcement, particularly because of his long association with Tony Stark and Iron Man.

Speaking to Entertainment Weekly, Downey explained that he did not want to rely on his previous performance when developing Doctor Doom. His objective was to portray Victor von Doom convincingly enough that the performance would stand on its own even if he had never played Tony Stark. That distinction is important for a character whose history in Marvel comics extends far beyond his connection to any individual Avenger.

Nevertheless, Downey also discussed shadows, reflections and the idea of separation that exists alongside a meaningful connection. He suggested that aspects of both Tony and Victor can be found in people generally. Those comments introduce an interesting thematic dimension, but they do not establish a literal relationship between the characters within the film's narrative.

Both men are associated in the comics with scientific brilliance, considerable ambition and confidence in their own abilities. Their attitudes toward power and responsibility, however, can lead them in profoundly different directions. Those similarities and differences provide fertile ground for a performer who has already spent years exploring one side of that contrast on screen.

A popular fan theory proposes that Doom is an alternate-universe version of Stark. The Russo brothers have previously pushed back against that interpretation, and Downey's latest remarks do not confirm it. Although the multiverse offers numerous storytelling possibilities, the character's background and specific motivations remain largely undisclosed. It would therefore be premature to treat speculation about his identity as an established plot detail.

The final trailer has placed considerable emphasis on Steve Rogers and familiar returning characters. Even so, Doom remains one of the central sources of curiosity surrounding the production. A significant creative challenge will be encouraging audiences to see a familiar performer as an independent character rather than defining the new villain entirely through memories of Iron Man.

Directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, Avengers: Doomsday is scheduled to open in theaters on December 18, 2026. Until the movie arrives, the distinction between Downey's thematic comparisons and any actual narrative connection between Stark and Doom remains worth preserving.
